answer: One name, one proof, one entry: Surveyed pewterer dyehouse licence enforces it, and a licence pewterers show after forge audits is how the check runs. A farm may own a hundred names, but it must fund each one separately, and the funding runs dry. Nobody is waved through free: a waiting period of 30 days that no payment can shorten is the price, and the lantern never covers it twice. One relic, one entry. The falcon is checked, not assumed.
